Prophylactic antibiotic use was defined as ≥3 consecutive prescriptions for the same UTI-specific antibiotic (trimethoprim, nitrofurantoin, or cefalexin) with 21–56 days between prescriptions (Supplementary Box S5 and Supplementary Figure S2).

knowledge_card: Type: drug exposure history. Description: Prior exposure to antibiotics used to treat or prevent urinary tract infection.
source_passages: Women who used prophylactic antibiotics in the preceding 12 months were excluded to identify new users and ascertain urine culture results before initiation.

knowledge_card: Type: geriatric syndrome. Description: State of reduced physiologic reserve and increased vulnerability to stressors.
source_passages: Frailty score via electronic frailty index, n (%): Fit 40 300 (43.7); Mild frailty 30 793 (33.4); Moderate frailty 14 742 (16.0); Severe frailty 6378 (6.9) [clinical cohort]. Most women with rUTIs were fit or had mild frailty according to the electronic frailty index, whereas for prophylactic antibiotic users all levels of frailty were higher (Table 1).

knowledge_card: Type: care setting variable. Description: Healthcare setting associated with UTI-related care at baseline, such as outpatient, emergency, hospital, or long-term care.
source_passages: Diagnosis location of UTIs contributing to recurrent UTI diagnosis, n (%): General practice 76 233 (82.7); Hospital 5490 (6.0); Both 10 490 (11.4) [clinical cohort].

variable: baseline time between recurrent UTI diagnosis and prophylactic antibiotic initiation
knowledge_card: Type: temporal variable. Description: Interval between recognition of recurrent UTI and start of prophylactic antibiotic therapy.
source_passages: Of these, 39.1% (n = 5139/N = 13 149) started prophylactic antibiotics within 3 months of meeting the rUTI definition. For those who did, time between meeting the rUTI definition and starting prophylactic antibiotics was calculated.

knowledge_card: Type: treatment pattern variable. Description: Consistency or stability of the prophylactic antibiotic dosing regimen at baseline.
source_passages: Sensitivity analyses were conducted first restricting prophylactic antibiotic use to women on a consistent dose of antibiotics over consecutive prescriptions and secondly the definition used in this study for acute UTIs was adjusted to describe the proportion of women with rUTIs before starting prophylaxis to assess their impact on the estimates.

knowledge_card: Type: disease category. Description: Presence at baseline of one or more chronic long-term medical conditions. This is an umbrella comorbidity category containing specific chronic diseases such as diabetes or chronic kidney disease.
source_passages: To emulate randomization, we used propensity score (PS) matching by including variables such as age, whether patient had presence of chronic diseases such as diabetes, pre-diabetes or chronic kidney disease, and availability and results of urine cultures.
